# Causal Impact analysis

## Staff sickness

```{r, include=TRUE}


# Find the best matches  
mm <- MarketMatching::best_matches(data=staff_sickness,
                   id_variable="organisation_code",
                   date_variable="month",
                   matching_variable="percent",
                   parallel=FALSE,
                   warping_limit=1, # warping limit=1
                   dtw_emphasis=1, # rely only on dtw for pre-screening
                   matches=2, # request 2 matches
                   start_match_period="2016-09-01",
                   end_match_period="2022-10-01")

#View the best matches
knitr::kable(head(mm$BestMatches))

results <- MarketMatching::inference(matched_markets = mm,
                                     analyze_betas=TRUE,
                                     test_market = "REM",
                                    end_post_period = "2023-10-01",
                                    alpha=0.05, 
                                    prior_level_sd=0.01,
                                    nseasons=12)

# Plot out actual vs expected
results$PlotActualVersusExpected

# Plot out cumulative effect
results$PlotCumulativeEffect

# Plot pointwise effect
results$PlotPointEffect

#Plot the actuals 
results$PlotActuals

# See which hospital receives the highest weight in determining the outcome
coeff <- results$Coefficients
knitr::kable(head(coeff))


```

```{r, include=FALSE}

#Store predicted values in dataframe
pred <- results$Predictions
knitr::kable(head(pred))

# Check out the DW and MAPE of the model
results$PlotPriorLevelSdAnalysis

#Prospective Pseudo Power Curves -will help you evaluate if your choice of test and control markets creates a sufficient model to measure a realistic lift from a future intervention. 

power <- MarketMatching::test_fake_lift(matched_markets = mm, 
                                      test_market = "REM", 
                                      end_fake_post_period = "2023-10-01", 
                                      prior_level_sd = 0.01, 
                                      steps=10,
                                      max_fake_lift=0.05)
#And plot the graph- Ideally, a curve that starts at high probability on the left side, reaches its minimum at zero lift, and then rises again symmetrically. If the curve does not reach its minimum at zero there may be systemic model bias in the post period. 
power$ResultsGraph


```

## RTT Waiting time data- Median waiting time (in weeks) 

```{r}


# Find the best matches  
mm <- MarketMatching::best_matches(rtt_data,
                   id_variable="organisation_code",
                   date_variable="month",
                   matching_variable="median_by_prov",
                   parallel=FALSE,
                   warping_limit=1, # warping limit=1
                   dtw_emphasis=1, # rely only on dtw for pre-screening
                   matches=2, # request 5 matches
                   start_match_period="2016-09-01",
                   end_match_period="2022-10-01")

#View the best matches
knitr::kable(head(mm$BestMatches))

results <- MarketMatching::inference(matched_markets = mm,
                                     analyze_betas=TRUE,
                                     test_market = "REM",
                                    end_post_period = "2023-10-01",
                                    alpha=0.05, 
                                    prior_level_sd=0.01,
                                    nseasons=12)

#Absolute Effect indicates an increase in the median of 0.94 relative to what we expected. The Relative Effect provides a standardized view, indicating a 0.94% increase in the median. Probability of a causal impact indicates that the likelihood of observing this effect by chance is high (e.g., 100 - 55.2). 

# Plot out actual vs expected
results$PlotActualVersusExpected

# Plot out cumulative effect
results$PlotCumulativeEffect

# Plot pointwise effect
results$PlotPointEffect

#Plot the actuals 
results$PlotActuals


# See which hospital recieves the highest weight in determining the outcome
coeff <- results$Coefficients
knitr::kable(head(coeff))



```

```{r, include=FALSE}

#Store predicted values in dataframe
pred <- results$Predictions
knitr::kable(head(pred))

# Check out the DW and MAPE of the model
results$PlotPriorLevelSdAnalysis

#Prospective Pseudo Power Curves -will help you evaluate if your choice of test and control markets creates a sufficient model to measure a realistic lift from a future intervention. 

power <- MarketMatching::test_fake_lift(matched_markets = mm, 
                                      test_market = "REM", 
                                      end_fake_post_period = "2023-10-01", 
                                      prior_level_sd = 0.01, 
                                      steps=10,
                                      max_fake_lift=0.05)
#And plot the graph- Ideally, a curve that starts at high probability on the left side, reaches its minimum at zero lift, and then rises again symmetrically. If the curve does not reach its minimum at zero there may be systemic model bias in the post period. 
power$ResultsGraph



```
